boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten campus places for focused work, group projects, commuter downtime, recreation, reflection and student-led outdoor activity.

cards.title: Settle Into the Renovated Fourth Floor
cards.subtitle: Booths, collaborative tables and research support inside Gumberg Library
cards.notes: Use a booth for laptop work, browse the Library of Things, or book the Research Huddle Room when a project needs librarian input.
cards.short_summary: A redesigned library floor combines flexible seating, collaborative work areas and research consultations.
cards.evidence_claim: Duquesne reports that Gumberg Library’s renovated fourth floor reopened in September 2025 with booths, collaborative study spaces, a Library of Things display and a Research Huddle Room.
cards.source_title: Gumberg Library Celebrates Reopening of Renovated Fourth Floor
cards.access_notes: The fourth floor is open to the Duquesne community; research appointments can be booked online.

cards.entity_name: Gumberg Library Glass Group Study Rooms
cards.title: Put the Group Around a Whiteboard
cards.subtitle: Reservable glass study rooms on Gumberg Library’s fifth floor
cards.notes: Reserve a room for three or more people, bring the confirmation, and scan the entrance QR code within 15 minutes to retain the booking.
cards.short_summary: These enclosed rooms give project groups a whiteboard, power access and a defined reservation window.
cards.evidence_claim: Gumberg Library lists fifth-floor Glass Group Study Rooms for groups of at least three, with whiteboards, power access and QR-code booking confirmation.
cards.source_title: Space Availability — Gumberg Library Study Rooms
cards.access_notes: Reservation required; confirm at the room within 15 minutes. Intended for groups of three or more students.

cards.title: Build a Project Around Shared Screens
cards.subtitle: Seven collaborative workspaces inside Gumberg Library
cards.notes: Bring a team assignment that benefits from working side by side; check library availability before relying on the classroom for unscheduled use.
cards.short_summary: A technology-oriented classroom provides seven defined work areas for collaborative learning.
cards.evidence_claim: Duquesne’s current undergraduate catalog states that Gumberg Library contains a FlexTech classroom with seven collaborative workspaces.
cards.access_notes: Availability may depend on scheduled instruction; consult Gumberg Library before planning a visit.

cards.title: Prototype a Lesson With Materials in Hand
cards.subtitle: A PreK–12 resource room within Gumberg Library
cards.notes: Use the books, games, puppets and teaching resources to shape a lesson or child-focused project; confirm service access with library staff.
cards.short_summary: This specialized resource room supports hands-on planning for students whose work involves children and education.
cards.evidence_claim: Duquesne identifies the Maureen P. Sullivan Curriculum Center as a PreK–12 resource room available to the campus community, with books, games, puppets and teaching materials.
cards.access_notes: Available to members of the campus community working with children; confirm current library service conditions.

cards.title: Read and Discuss Among Specialized Collections
cards.subtitle: A first-floor research center in Gumberg Library
cards.notes: Consult the specialized holdings for philosophy research, or submit the reservation form at least one week ahead for an eligible academic gathering.
cards.short_summary: A named special-collections center doubles as a setting for lectures, defenses, conferences and meetings.
cards.evidence_claim: Duquesne places the Simon Silverman Phenomenology Center on Gumberg Library’s first floor and permits reservation requests for lectures, conferences, defenses and meetings.
cards.access_notes: Event reservation requests must be submitted at least one week in advance; collection access may have separate procedures.

cards.title: Make a Between-Class Base in the Union
cards.subtitle: A lounge and kitchenette for commuter students on the Union’s first floor
cards.notes: Charge devices, use the kitchenette and reset between classes here; treat the room as a commuter resource rather than an unrestricted visitor lounge.
cards.short_summary: The Commuter Center gives off-campus students a practical campus base with seating and everyday facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: Duquesne states that the first-floor Commuter Center contains comfortable lounge furniture, a kitchenette, a computer lab and additional commuter resources.
cards.access_notes: Located on the first floor of the Duquesne Union and intended for commuter and off-campus students.

cards.title: Turn a Commuter Break Into Group Work
cards.subtitle: Computers, printing and meeting displays in Duquesne Union Room 112
cards.notes: Bring classmates here when a project needs a computer, printer or shared display; allow time to find another space if equipment is occupied.
cards.short_summary: A commuter-focused collaboration room supports quick study sessions and small-team work between classes.
cards.evidence_claim: Duquesne identifies the Commuter Collaboration Commons in Union Room 112 and says it offers computers, a printer and meeting displays for collaboration or study.
cards.access_notes: Located in Duquesne Union Room 112 and presented as a resource for commuter students.

cards.title: Change the Pace on Four Fitness Floors
cards.subtitle: Card-access recreation space in the Power Center
cards.notes: Use the track, courts or fitness areas for a study break, and check the current operating schedule before walking over during holidays or summer.
cards.short_summary: The campus recreation center gathers cardio equipment, weights, courts, studios and an indoor track in one facility.
cards.evidence_claim: Duquesne describes the Power Recreation Center as an 80,000-square-foot facility with cardio equipment, courts, studios, weights and an indoor track.
cards.access_notes: Card-controlled campus recreation facility for eligible Duquesne students and employees; hours and holiday closures vary.

cards.title: Join the Ecology Club at the Pollinator Garden
cards.subtitle: A student-maintained garden beside Academic Walk near College Hall
cards.notes: Pause to observe the plantings, or email Environmental Science to ask about participating instead of assuming that unscheduled garden work is permitted.
cards.short_summary: This visible Academic Walk garden connects a small outdoor campus space with student-led ecological stewardship.
cards.evidence_claim: Duquesne says its pollinator garden is adjacent to Academic Walk near College Hall and is maintained by the student Ecology Club.
cards.access_notes: Email the university’s Environmental Science contact to ask about organized involvement.

cards.title: Leave a Quiet Interval at the Grotto
cards.subtitle: A campus space for private prayer and contemplation since 1956
cards.notes: Visit for a brief quiet pause, keep conversation low and yield space to anyone using the grotto for prayer or personal contemplation.
cards.short_summary: The long-standing campus grotto offers a defined outdoor setting for stillness and individual reflection.
cards.evidence_claim: Duquesne states that Our Lady of Lourdes Grotto has served as a campus space for private prayer and contemplation since 1956.
cards.access_notes: Use respectfully as a prayer and contemplation space; the source does not publish specific access hours.
